contexts.text: From those in hatred and revenge exhale spheres which cause a swoon...
Heavenly light falls into their smoky lumen... some of them fall as it were into a swoon.
(When in that Heaven) they began to fall into a holy swoon.
When (the celestial Angels) are sent to others, they are encompassed by other Angels; (for otherwise) the sphere of their love would throw into a swoon those to whom they are sent...
There are Spirits who inject unclean colds... they also induce swoons.
I then felt a pain in my head, such as is felt by those who fall into a swoon. DMin 4686.
As they prevented the influx of the Angels, so the life of thought... became at last as with those who fall into a swoon.
(In the Third Earth) if a man persists in evil, he dies by a swoon. SE 1682.
An evil Spirit, when merely looked at by the Angels, falls into a swoon.
When good Spirits... perceive the heavenly joy from an Angel... they are filled with such delight that they come as it were into a sweet swoon.
If an Angel of the Ultimate Heaven... enters the Third Heaven, he falls as it were into a swoon. Explained.
(The exhalations) from the poisonous Hells induce swoons.
So long as the heart moves, love with its vital heat remains and preserves life, as is evident from swoons, suffocations, and embryos. DLW 399:2. DLW 410. DWis 3. 5. DWis 7. 4. 2. DWis 10. 7.
That man has neither sensitive nor active life without the cooperation of the heart and lungs, is evident from swoons, when the heart alone acts. DWis 6:end.
They then appear to themselves to fall into a swoon... and sink down into their Hell.
When man wishes to perceive... the eternity of God before times, it is as if his mind fell into a swoon...
Then the head, having no correspondence with the body, falls into a swoon.
If the conjunction between men and Angels were severed... the men would instantly fall into a swoon... and if it were not restored, they would die.
I perceived the same stench by a kind of swoon...
If they try to return, they fall into a swoon, from the anguish.
6. a. The heart and lungs are separated in swoons and suffocations; but, when separated, they do not make the life of man's body...
